samples.question: This page shows one solid dark reef of blocky outline, together with grey, blue, orange, red and green decorations that lie on the open page away from the reef. Only the dark reef ink and the white paper decide the answer; the coloured decorations never count and never block anything. White paper cut into the reef forms pools. A pool is shut when dark reef ink encloses it completely, so that no white route leads from that pool out to the open page around the reef; a pool that reaches the open page through a white gap in the reef is an open notch, and an open notch never counts, no matter how large it looks or how deep it cuts. Take the shut pools only. Compare the white area of the single largest shut pool with the summed white area of every other shut pool. Areas are compared as they are drawn, and the reef is drawn on a coarse block grid, so no shut pool is a borderline sliver. How much dark ink the reef carries, how many shut pools there are, how large the reef is, where the reef sits on the page, how deep the open notches cut, and which colours appear never decide the answer by themselves. Is the largest shut pool larger in white area than all the other shut pools put together? Answer yes or no.
